subject: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@procurecorp.com, mary@edge.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact

Team —

Short version: Research validated Halo-XL-13B variants show a consistent 18–23% token-cost reduction and 12–18% latency improvement on our P-1000 infra for 512–1024 seq workflows. Edge AI (mary@edge.ai) is pushing to move their pilot to Dedicated in Q2 and procurement is asking whether we can onboard earlier than our normal 6-week intake because they need a pinned version for contract sign-off.

Ask: Id like to request a provisional version-pin exemption for Halo-XL (variant set: halo-xl-13b, halo-xl-13b-q4x, halo-xl-13b-int8) for a two-week window to enable a limited canary in staging -> small Dedicated pool. During that window well run the telem gating and the canary rollback plan.

Why: this variant delivers material cost/perf win for the Edge AI workload and could convert their pilot to a paid Dedicated contract (DEAL-7842). Were balancing speed -> revenue vs our standard stability gate.

Known risks: tokenizer parity quirk (observed in a subset of BPE edge cases), slightly different KV cache growth pattern under long-chat sessions, and missing a small slice of token-level telemetry for the int8 path. Attached are quick artifacts: compat-check-log.txt and telemetry-gap-summary.pdf.

Request details:
- Duration: 14 calendar days provisional pin (then revert unless full intake passes)
- Scope: staging + one small Dedicated pool (up to 4 GPUs) + 5% canary of incoming QA traffic
- Telemetry: enforced gating in Redwood Console (token-error-rate, hallucination-rate on our eval set, latency p95)
- Rollback: immediate unpin -> route to stable-13b fallback, deprioritize autoscaler bursts for the canary pool

Marissa (for Ops)
Marissa Cole
Manager, Model Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compat-check-log.txt (text), telemetry-gap-summary.pdf (summary)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. Im supportive of exploring a short provisional window but calling out technical blockers well need to own during the canary: 

1) Tokenizer parity: the BPE edge cases you mentioned surfaced in our smoke tests (see line ~172 in compat-check-log.txt). That leads to a small but measurable drift in token counts for a small percentage (<0.5%) of prompts. For billing/quotas this could be noisy. We need a compensating layer in the ingestion path to normalize token counting for the canary so billing metrics don't explode.

2) int8 path telemetry: telemetry-gap-summary.pdf flagged that we lack per-op memory metrics for the int8 kernels on our P-1000 build. For an int8 variant we should be careful about eviction under memory pressure; I recommend we disable aggressive batch fusion for the canary to avoid OOM edgecases.

3) KV cache behavior: naomi, can you run the long-chat 3k-step session test with the new checkpoint and capture cache growth and perf deltas? If growth patterns differ we may need a config tweak to the cache evictor.

If we can agree on compensations above, Id approve a 10–14 day provisional window. Ops will prepare the small Dedicated pool and gating hooks. We should also add a KPI that forces automatic rollback if token-error-rate > 0.8% or p95 latency regresses > 20% vs stable-13b.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact

Appreciate the thorough callout. A few product considerations from my side before I sign off: 

- Customer impact: Mary, can you confirm whether Edge AI absolutely requires pinned variant for contract signing, or would a staged SLA (pilot SLA + later pin) work? Wed prefer the latter to reduce risk.
- Roadmap clash: We have a stability-focused sprint scheduled week of Mar 13 that touches routing fallbacks and billing normalization. If we do this canary now, we risk scope overlap. Can we shift the canary to finish before that sprint or push the sprint by one week?
- Metrics: we need a clear revenue gate tied to canary—e.g., if we can demonstrate 10% lower per-token bill in the canary pool for Edges workload, we prioritize final intake. Otherwise revert.

Im neutral but leaning yes if Karthik and Naomi can provide tight mitigations and Ops can run the exact gating. Marissa, can you propose a one-week timeline for the canary start + runbook and loop legal/procurement for contract language?

-Laura
Product Lead, Model Platform
Redwood Inference

To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact

Quick results from the extended tests (attached: halo-smoke-results.csv) — summary below: 

- Tokenizer parity: Confirmed drift occurs for ~0.42% of corpus. Drift manifests as off-by-1 token in 85% of those cases and off-by-2 in the remainder. The mismatches correlate with a legacy BPE merge behavior present in the upstream tokenizer release. Workaround: apply a normalization pass during tokenization for canary requests (cheap, ~0.5ms median overhead).

- KV cache: Long-chat 3k-step run shows a steady linear growth until step ~1800 and then a plateau. Growth is ~5% higher memory footprint vs stable-13b for identical prompts; no functional correctness issues observed. Rafael, for the Dedicated pool we should raise the default cache eviction threshold by 8% for this variant.

- int8 telemetry: We captured memory high-water marks but still missing per-kernel accounting on the P-1000 driver. Doing an interim sampling every 30s gives us enough signal for the canary gates. Ops: enable sampling and surface the metric in Redwood Console.

Ive uploaded the CSV and added a short runbook snippet to the Google Doc (link above) with config diffs for the canary. If we normalize token counts and adjust the cache evictor, the canary looks safe for 10–14 days.

-naomi
Senior Research Engineer, Performance
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Halo-XL onboarding: provisional pin exemption request & product impact (final ask)

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick recap and next steps so legal/procurement/ops have a single artifact to act on: 

1) Duration: 12 days provisional pin starting Mar 8 00:00 UTC -> Mar 20 00:00 UTC (adjusted to finish before product sprint).
2) Scope: staging + Dedicated canary pool (4x P-1000) with 5% canary traffic, Edge AI workload only.
3) Mitigations agreed: token normalization pass at ingestion (Karthik), disable aggressive batch fusion on int8 path (Karthik), cache eviction threshold +8% (Rafael), 30s telemetry sampling for int8 (Naomi).
4) Hard KPIs for auto-rollback: token-error-rate > 0.8% OR p95 latency regression > 20% vs stable-13b OR any OOM in Dedicated pool.
5) Revenue gate: if canary shows >=10% per-token cost reduction for Edge AI across the 12-day window, we proceed to full intake and legal will include a provisional pin clause in the SOW.

Mary: can procurement/contract language be OK with a provisional pin clause that auto-reverts after the canary unless both sides sign final SOW? procure@procurecorp.com, looping you to confirm the ask on your side.

If everyone is good, please reply with a single-line sign-off by EOD today so Ops can start provisioning on Mar 7 (dry-run) and we begin the canary on Mar 8.

Marissa
Manager, Model Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: halo-smoke-results.csv (summary)
